input.content:
**What**: Exploration of slugify('Crème Brûlée') -> 'crème-brûlée' bug.
**Why**: Root cause in src/slugify.js line 10: /[^\p{L}\p{N}]+/gu keeps accented letters (\p{L}), so diacritics are never folded. Only 3 ASCII tests exist in test/slugify.test.js; no diacritic test. Node >=26, vitest 3.2.4.
ASSUMED ANSWERS (unattended): goal=bugfix; ASCII behaviour unchanged; no new deps; backward compat for non-Latin scripts desirable.
**Approaches**:
A (recommended) NFD normalize + strip \p{M} before the existing replace: str.normalize('NFD').replace(/\p{M}+/gu,''). Low complexity, no deps, ASCII untouched (NFD is identity on ASCII). Con: does not fold ß, ø, æ, đ, ł (no decomposition) -> they stay as letters. Note: Indic combining marks are already treated as separators today, so stripping them is a no-op change in effect for separators vs. removal (could differ: marks previously became '-', now removed - minor behaviour change for such scripts). Hangul decomposes to jamo under NFD; use NFC re-normalize after stripping to be safe.
B A + small explicit map for non-decomposing Latin letters (ß->ss, æ->ae, ø->o, đ->d, ł->l, œ->oe). Medium-low complexity; more complete for European text; map needs maintenance.
C Add a dependency (e.g. slugify / transliteration lib). Most complete (CJK, Cyrillic transliteration) but adds dep to a 'tiny' lib, changes behaviour for non-Latin scripts, higher risk.
**Where**: src/slugify.js, test/slugify.test.js (add tests: 'Crème Brûlée'->'creme-brulee', ASCII regressions, maybe 'Ünïcödé', combining-char input), README.md optional note.
**Recommendation**: A, with NFC re-normalize after stripping; B as optional follow-up.

## ASSUMED ANSWERs (unattended run, no questions asked)
- Approach: A (NFD, strip combining marks, NFC, then existing pipeline).

## Intent
slugify('Crème Brûlée') returns 'crème-brûlée' because src/slugify.js line 10 (/[^\p{L}\p{N}]+/gu) keeps accented letters as \p{L}. URL slugs should fold Latin diacritics to base letters ('creme-brulee').

Stripping all \p{M} would corrupt non-Latin scripts whose vowel signs or marks are \p{M} (Devanagari, Thai, Arabic harakat). The final NFC recomposes any non-Latin sequences that NFD decomposed (e.g. Hangul), so non-Latin output stays identical to today.

# Proposal: fix-slugify-diacritics

## ASSUMED ANSWERs (unattended run, no questions asked)
- Approach: A (NFD, strip combining marks, NFC, then existing pipeline).
- No new dependencies. ASCII output unchanged. Non-Latin letters kept as today.
- Scope: slugify only. Risk tolerance: conservative. Gate auto-approved.

## Intent
slugify('Crème Brûlée') returns 'crème-brûlée' because src/slugify.js line 10 (/[^\p{L}\p{N}]+/gu) keeps accented letters as \p{L}. URL slugs should fold Latin diacritics to base letters ('creme-brulee').

## Scope - In
- In src/slugify.js: after toLowerCase/trim, apply str.normalize('NFD'), remove combining diacritical marks, then normalize('NFC'), then the existing replace pipeline.
- Strip only the Combining Diacritical Marks block (/[̀-ͯ]/g), NOT all \p{M}. Stripping all \p{M} would corrupt non-Latin scripts whose vowel signs or marks are \p{M} (Devanagari, Thai, Arabic harakat). The final NFC recomposes any non-Latin sequences that NFD decomposed (e.g. Hangul), so non-Latin output stays identical to today.
- New tests in test/slugify.test.js: 'Crème Brûlée' -> 'creme-brulee'; 'Åñö' -> 'ano'; already-decomposed input; non-Latin unchanged (e.g. Cyrillic 'Привет мир', Hangul); ASCII regression (existing 3 tests).
- README.md slugify note, if it describes behavior.

## Scope - Out
- Transliteration of non-Latin scripts; folding of ligatures/special letters (ß, æ, ø, đ, ł do not decompose under NFD and remain as-is); new dependencies (e.g. slugify, diacritics libs); options/API changes; other textkit functions; src/index.js exports.

## Approach
Add a normalization step before the existing regex. Single-line pipeline change, no signature change. Details (constant naming, regex literal) are left to Design.
